summary:
Caraga's only region-specific signal in the sourced material is a non-discrimination ordinance adopted by Butuan City in 2016. Butuan City is the regional capital, and the ordinance places it among the Philippine localities that supply non-discrimination coverage on grounds including sexual orientation and gender identity through a local instrument rather than a national statute.

No other Caraga-specific law, regulation, enforcement practice or documented incident bearing on trans people was recorded in the inventory. A visitor to Caraga otherwise stands under the national framework of the Philippines.
tangentialFactors:
The Butuan City ordinance dates from 2016, and comparable municipal and provincial non-discrimination measures have continued to be adopted elsewhere in the Philippines, so the capital's instrument sits within a wider pattern of local provision in the absence of a national statute.

The sourced material does not establish whether any other locality in Caraga has followed Butuan City. Coverage across the rest of the region is therefore open rather than absent, and the ordinance's practical weight for a visitor depends on how the city's own administration applies it.
localsOnly:
Butuan City residents have a local non-discrimination ordinance adopted in 2016 to rely on, which residents may invoke in a way that is not available in Philippine localities without such an instrument.

The sourced material does not record the ordinance's protected grounds in full, the complaint route it establishes, the penalties it carries, or any case in which it has been enforced. Resident-facing recourse under it is therefore documented as existing but not described.
outOfScopeNotes:
The text, scope, protected grounds and enforcement machinery of the Butuan City ordinance are not reproduced in the inventory; the claim sourced is its existence and 2016 date. Whether it reaches services, employment, accommodation or public facilities is unresolved on the available sources.

No enforcement data, complaints, prosecutions or incidents involving trans people in Caraga appear anywhere in the inventory. Absence of records here is not evidence of absence of events.

The source dedicated to Caraga itself returned no usable finding for this jurisdiction, so every region-level statement above rests on the single locality-level entry.

Whether Caraga's other provinces and cities have adopted non-discrimination or SOGI ordinances is not sourced and should be verified independently.
